firstFinal:
I ran a red proof of the old test file against the current code, in a temporary checkout. It confirms the old test depended on `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`, and the fixed test doesn't. The command was `squeal proof scripts/release-identity.test.mjs --base 936cbecf --case test --env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2 --env GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`.

**Why the old test leaked.** In `936cbecf`, the `run()` helper in `scripts/release-identity.test.mjs` stripped the ambient environment with `/^(CEZ_|HSQ_|GITHUB_ACTIONS$|…)/`. That removes only `GITHUB_ACTIONS`. It also no longer set `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` itself. So whatever `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` the workflow supplied passed straight into the release script.

**What the proof showed.** The red side (old test, `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`, as on a CI re-run) failed. The nightly and PR release cases, shown here, each gave a version with a `.2` suffix:
- Nightly: `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9.2` instead of `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9`.
- PR: `1.2.3-pr7.9.2` instead of `1.2.3-pr7.9`.

**Why the fixed test doesn't depend on it.** The fix in `50d4ce31` makes two changes:
- It widens the filter back to `GITHUB_`, so every ambient `GITHUB_*` variable is stripped.
- It sets `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` explicitly in the child environment.

The green side (the fixed test at HEAD, run under the same injected `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`) passed. The same test also passes without the injected variables. The result was 1 proven, 0 not red, 0 not green.

The "old" test here is the `936cbecf` version, which is the one the last commit replaced. That commit was a partial revert of it, and the change in `936cbecf` is what introduced the dependency. I did not edit anything in the tree.
